instruction: Configure a plain text email signature in Thunderbird. First line should be "Dr. Emily Chen", second line "Research Institute", and third line "Department of AI".

mail.identity.id1.htmlSigText.ref: Dr. Emily Chen\nResearch Institute\nDepartment of AI

metadata.explanation: Three-line signature format. Similar complexity to original but with additional line. Evaluator checks prefs.js for the multi-line signature text.
metadata.verification: Reuses existing check_thunderbird_prefs metric. Signature text verified to match regex escape requirements for special characters (dots, plus signs).

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic error: Instruction requires 'plain text email signature' but evaluator checks 'mail.identity.id1.htmlSigText' which is the HTML signature preference key
For plain text signatures, Thunderbird typically uses 'mail.identity.id1.sig_file' (file path) or stores plain text signatures differently than HTML signatures
The evaluator cannot correctly verify whether a plain text signature was configured, as it checks the wrong preference type
Postconfig correctly closes Thunderbird to flush preferences to disk (good practice)
Expected value format with \n escaping is correct for regex matching, but applied to wrong preference key
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change instruction to 'Configure an HTML email signature' to match what the evaluator checks, OR
Change evaluator to check the correct Thunderbird preference for plain text signatures (investigate which preference key Thunderbird uses for plain text signatures)
Verify in actual Thunderbird documentation or prefs.js which preference stores plain text vs HTML signatures
Consider checking both signature file path and inline text preferences depending on how Thunderbird stores plain text signatures
